quandoUsar: Confirming a destructive action, such as deleting a project, explaining the consequences in `description`.
A short form that must be completed or canceled before returning to the page.
Decisions that cannot go unnoticed: the backdrop darkens with a blur and the page behind becomes inaccessible until the dialog closes.
quandoEvitar: Use `drawer` for longer tasks where people still want to see the page beside it.
Use `popover` for contextual information that does not need to block the page.
Use `confirm-morph` or `hold-to-confirm` to confirm a destructive action on the button itself, without opening a window.

teclado.acao: Move through the dialog controls without leaving it; on open, focus goes to the first control, the close button.
Closes the dialog and returns focus to the `DialogTrigger`.

acessibilidade: Radix modal dialog: `role="dialog"` with `title` as its name (an `<h2>`) and `description` as its description; the rest of the page leaves the accessibility tree and scrolling is locked.
Focus is trapped in the dialog and returns to the trigger on close; the close button is named “Close dialog”, fixed in English in the code.
To send initial focus to another control, use `onOpenAutoFocus` on `DialogContent`, which forwards the Radix props.
movimento: The backdrop fades in with a 7 px blur while the panel rises 8 px and grows from 96% on a no-overshoot spring; closing is shorter and starts from wherever the entrance is.
If `title` or `description` change while the dialog is open, the new text rises and the old one exits upward.
With “reduce motion” on, backdrop and panel only fade, in 120 ms.
responsivo: The panel is up to 440 px wide (the screen minus 2rem on phones) with a maximum height of `100dvh` minus 2rem, scrolling inside when the content exceeds that.
notasIA: Assemble `Dialog`, `DialogTrigger asChild` around the button, and `DialogContent` with `title`; buttons that close go in `DialogClose asChild`. Import from `@/components/ryan-ui/dialog/dialog`.
To close after an async action, control it with `open` and `onOpenChange` and pass `false` when it finishes, as the demo does.
Use this file's `Dialog` as the root: under a plain Radix `Root`, `DialogContent` animates with CSS keyframes, without the Motion spring.
